items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I found out the name of this trumpet player later... His name was Freddie Jenkins... The strong man of the band was Freddie Jenkins... I had not heard too many trumpet players except... Freddie Jenkins

ctx.x: As bus boy at this restaurant in the zoo I heard many concerts because the summer concerts took place on the stage of an open air theatre just in front of where the people would eat this was also open air. I remember particularly the anvil chorus and a man that played xylophones which impressed me so much that I started looking at the prices of some in a Sears and Roebuck catalogue.

There was a dance hall a few feet in the back of the restaurant and one night I heard a trumpet sound coming from there that I had not heard before at this dance hall. When I had the chance I walked over there to see who it could be and there was a little negro boy playing trumpet with his left hand. It was the first time I had ever seen a negro musician sitting in with a white orchestra at the zoo or any place else in Cincinnati and I knew this youngster was good because he sounded good and had to be, to be…

I stopped working at the zoo restaurant after a few months. I never stayed on any job very long and always found an excuse to tell my father the reason I quit. My father had a little round savings bank that would hold only ten cent
